newsitem.title: ESTONIA: NEW GOVT PRESENTED TO PRESIDENT, TO BE DECIDED.
newsitem.headline: NEW GOVT PRESENTED TO PRESIDENT, TO BE DECIDED.

text.p: Estonia's prime ministerial candidate Mart Siimann on Friday presented his proposed goverment to the president but was still awaiting his approval, a spokesman for the president's office said.
Siimann presented his proposed government to President Lennart Meri at 1900/1700 GMT on Friday but at 2345/2145GMT approval was yet to be given.
"The president has not yet announced his decision," spokesman Ando Noormets told Reuters.
Under the Estonian Constitution, the president has three days to make a decision on the appointment of a prime minister and his proposed government once the line-up is presented.
He was given the authority by parliament on Wednesday to form a new government and had to present his proposed government to the president within seven days.
Siimann, 50, is expected to replace veteran politician Tiit Vaehi who stepped down last month after 22 months in office.
Vaehi's resignation came after he only narrowly won a no confidence motion in parliament amid allegations he was involved in shady privatisation deals involving real estate.
Siimann, a former television and radio station manager, is the leader of the parliamentary faction of the Coalition Party which is one of the two largest groups in parliament.
No major changes are expected to the cabinet but the Education Minister Rein Loik has resigned for personal reasons and the position of Agriculture Minister was in some doubt.
Siimann has already assured the country that his government would continue the previous government's economic policies and reforms.
"The new government sees its mission in continuing the reforms," Siimann told parliament on Wednesday.
